requirements.name: Phased-array / beamforming signal processing

lines.quote: specifically, towed-array beamforming for hydrophone arrays ranging from 32 to 128 elements
I designed the beamspace transform that Baltic's 128-element towed array currently runs in production, and published the underlying algorithm in JNAS in 2019.
Efficient Frequency-Domain Coherence Estimation for Passive Acoustic Monitoring in Shallow Water
The paper presented an adaptive coherence method that improved detection reliability for low-SNR targets in Baltic's shallow-water monitoring application.

requirements.note: The cover letter attributes a 128-element towed-array beamspace-transform design to the 2019 JNAS publication and describes towed-array/hydrophone-array work not mentioned anywhere in the CV; the CV describes the same 2019 JNAS paper as being about frequency-domain coherence estimation for passive acoustic monitoring, unrelated to a beamspace transform or towed array, and the CV's only named project (the harbour monitoring demonstrator) is receiver front-end characterisation, not array beamforming. Both descriptions of what the published work covers cannot straightforwardly be true together; this extraction does not resolve which is accurate.

lines.quote: Maintained and extended Baltic's in-house embedded DSP library for the TI C5535 platform: approximately 12,000 lines of C covering FFT, FIR/IIR filtering, and spectral-estimation routines.
I wrote the original spectral module and have been the primary maintainer of the full library since 2017.

I wrote the production data-acquisition and processing pipeline for Baltic's harbour monitoring demonstrator entirely in Python — instrument control, real-time data ingestion from multiple channels, automated quality checks, and archival.
It is about 5,000 lines, fully tested, and has been running in production since the demonstrator deployed in 2021.

requirements.name: RF measurement experience
requirements.note: The frequency-domain characterisation work described uses a dynamic signal analyser on the acoustic receiver's analogue front end, not the RF network analysers, spectrum analysers, or anechoic-chamber work named by this requirement.

lines.quote: Published a peer-reviewed paper in the Journal of the Northern Acoustics Society (2019)
co-authored with colleagues at Baltic and the Aurajoki University.
Finnish permanent resident (Czech national), working in Finland since 2014 with no restrictions on EU employment.
Wrote the processing pipeline documentation and the 40-page final project report in English for the EU Kestrel-funded programme that contracted the demonstrator.

ask_in_screening.question: Can you describe any hands-on RF test-bench experience, such as network analysers, spectrum analysers, or anechoic-chamber measurement, if any?
